newsitem.title: USA: Ruggiero wants trade help for developing countries.
newsitem.headline: Ruggiero wants trade help for developing countries.

text.p: World Trade Organization (WTO) head Renato Ruggiero said on Monday he would like to see a ministerial trade meeting in Singapore in December take action to help the world's poorest countries.
This would include eliminating all tariffs and non-tariff barriers on least-developed country exports, and improving the investment climate they face.
"I see a commitment to action along these lines as a very important objective for Singapore," he told ministers at the annual meeting of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank.
The WTO is pushing for a trade initiatve to accompany a debt relief initiative agreed to this weekend by the IMF and World Bank to help the world's poorest nations.

Ruggiero, however, played down the possibility of dramatic decisions in Singapore, the first ministerial meeting of the Geneva-based trade watchdog, which replaced the GATT after Uruguay Round negotiations to liberalize world trade.
The meeting, he said, "is not the end of a negotiation, nor the launching of a new Round, but a very important point in a continuing process."
He acknowledged the difficulties of agreeing on new rules to liberalize investment -- which would lift barriers preventing foreign companies investing in some countries.

"The treatment of investment in the multilateral system is still a difficult issue in Geneva, but there seems to be a broad level of agreement that further work is needed -- if not on where it should take place," he said.
The most difficult issue, he said, was over labor standards -- which prohibit forced labor by prisoners, child labor and promote free association of workers.
France and the United States have pushed to make a link between respect for core labor standards and trade by getting the issue included on the agenda for the Singapore talks.
But other countries fiercely oppose the link with trade, accusing France and the United States of seeking to protect their own workers against cheaper labor abroad.
Ruggiero noted that all countries backed respect for core labor standards and that the competitive advantage of low-wage countries had not been called into question.

"I do not pretend that even on the basis of these elements, it will be easy to reach a consensus on this issue, but it is vital that it not become a divisive or disruptive point at Singapore," he said.
He also said he hoped for an agreement in Singapore on moves to end tariffs on information technology products.
